text:
- 1. Grealish returns after four games missed David Moyes has confirmed Jack Grealish is fit and available for Everton’s visit to Brentford on Monday after his recent disciplinary breach. Grealish missed Everton’s past four games mainly as a consequence of missing training before last month’s Carabao Cup win over Newcastle. His last appearance for the team was in the 2-0 loss to Chelsea on 17 October, but Moyes is now prepared to welcome the playmaker back into the fold. “He’s back in training and back in around the team,” the Everton manager said. The 31-year-old played in a behind-closed-doors fixture against Derby last week and apologised on social media for being unable to help the team, who have performed well in his absence. Moyes said of the apology: “I don’t do social media but I’ve heard about it.” Asked whether he had received a similar apology from Grealish in person, the Everton manager added: “We’ve just been getting on with our work. We’ve got a lot of other players here who we need to focus on as well, I can’t just concentrate on one player, and I’ve been trying to make sure everybody gets the right preparation for our next game against Brentford.” The Scot backed Jordan Pickford to respond strongly to the threat from James Trafford to his England place after the Leeds goalkeeper’s inclusion and impressive display in the Nations League win over Spain. “I don’t think it will have a great effect on him,” claimed Moyes. “If you’re playing for England you will always have other players chasing you. I still think Jordan Pickford is out there on his own at the moment. If anything, he’s getting better. It will be good for us now that he’s getting competition [with England].” Andy Hunter
- 2. Maresca backs Fernández but hints at tweaks Enzo Maresca has said he may need to tweak the balance of Manchester City’s midfield amid their faltering Premier League form. City went into the November international break on the back of three consecutive defeats in the league, having begun the campaign with seven wins on the bounce. Maresca’s side are third in the table, six points off leaders Arsenal, and face Fulham at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday. Maresca defended Enzo Fernández, whose performances have prompted debate over his best position and whether he leaves City’s team unbalanced. Maresca has mostly opted to play the £125m signing from Chelsea deeper in midfield alongside fellow summer recruit Elliot Anderson, with the more defensive-minded Ayyoub Bouaddi, who also arrived in the summer, largely a substitute. “For sure there are things we need to do better in terms of balance,” Maresca said. “But the same midfield that won seven games in a row is the same midfield that lost three games in a row. “We won games with Enzo, we lost games with Enzo. I know that when there is a defeat, we are all looking for the reason why. Sometimes we probably need more balance, we need different kinds of players. [It] depends a little bit on the game. The idea is to continue in attack in the same way, creating chances, but finding a balance when we defend.” Maresca also dismissed the notion that any uncertainty surrounding City’s financial case with the Premier League has negatively affected recent performances. It has been nearly two months since City were found guilty of more than 100 charges related to breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules, and they are waiting for the outcome of their appeal. All three of City’s league defeats have come since the ruling. “I don’t think the players are thinking too much about the noise,” Maresca said. “I don’t think they are worried about it.” Dominic Booth
- 3. Iraola: drone filming ‘shouldn’t be legal’ Andoni Iraola believes Manchester United have an advantage on Sunday with Mauricio Pochettino set to take charge of his first game but criticised unauthorised drone footage of the Argentinian’s first training session. Pochettino faces a daunting maiden outing when United travel to face Liverpool at Anfield. A drone operator apologised after posting a 12-minute video from Carrington on YouTube – since removed – which Liverpool head coach Iraola said he has seen. “Yesterday they were sending me the footage but I think the important part of this is it shouldn’t be legal,” said the Spaniard. “It happened to United but it could happen today to me. Yesterday you had access to our training, the cameras recorded also 15, 20 minutes of our training, you know who trained with us, you know who didn’t train. We know the same but it’s not a matter of the advantage, I think it’s the fact someone can do this. I think there is a reason we train behind closed doors because there are some things you have to respect and I don’t think it’s nice for any club.” With Pochettino having left his role as US boss to take charge at Old Trafford, there will be a considerable element of the unknown for Liverpool. He added of former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Pochettino: “We’ve faced each other and obviously he has a lot of Premier League games behind him that we can look at, we can look at games from the US. But it’s true they have this small advantage that we don’t have references to prepare because they can go different ways that we don’t know right now.” Liverpool have been boosted by the news Virgil van Dijk, Ryan Gravenberch and Jeremie Frimpong are all set to be available, while the international break has seen long-term absentees Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni take a step forward. Press Association
digest_he:
הקשר ג'ק גריליש החלים מהשעיה פנימית עקב עבירת משמעת וצפוי לחזור לסגל של אברטון לקראת המשחק מול ברנטפורד. המאמן דייוויד מויס אישר את כשירותו וציין כי השחקן הביע התנצלות פומבית על היעדרותו. במקביל, מויס הביע אמון בשוער ג'ורדן פיקפורד מול התחרות המתגברת בנבחרת אנגליה.

בגזרת מנצ'סטר סיטי, המאמן אנצו מרסקה הודה כי ייתכן שיידרשו שינויים באיזון חוליית הקישור לאחר שלושה הפסדי ליגה רצופים. מרסקה הגן על ביצועיו של אנצו פרננדז והבהיר כי חוסר היציבות אינו קשור לרעשי הרקע סביב ההליכים המשפטיים של המועדון מול הפרמייר ליג.

בנושא אחר, מאמן ליברפול אנדוני איראולה ביקר בחריפות את השימוש הלא חוקי ברחפנים שצילמו את אימוני מנצ'סטר יונייטד לקראת משחק הבכורה של המאמן החדש מאוריציו פוצ'טינו. איראולה טען כי מדובר במעשה שאינו צריך להיות חוקי, למרות שליברפול תקבל בחזרה מספר שחקני מפתח לקראת המפגש הישיר.
